context: area network · substations + MV rings + LV feeders; energised ring by ring, authority inspection per stage

brief.intro: New to this project type? A distribution network takes power from the primary substation and delivers it to every plot. Medium-voltage (11–33 kV) cables run in rings through a number of small distribution substations — a ring main unit, a transformer and a low-voltage panel in a kiosk or a room — and from each substation low-voltage feeders run to feeder pillars and on to the customers' meters. There are many small, similar pieces rather than one big one. The programme is driven by the delivery of transformers and switchgear, by the cable trenches (which must fit in with the other utilities and the roads), and by the power authority: it inspects each stage and it alone energises the network, ring by ring.

must_get_right: Get the design approved by the power authority before ordering — transformer ratings, RMU type and cable sizes are theirs to accept, and they will not energise anything they did not approve.
Transformers, RMUs and LV panels are the long-lead items; substation plinths or rooms must be ready and the equipment must be on site before the ring can be closed.
Coordinate the cable corridor with the other utilities and install road-crossing ducts before the road base — power cable is usually one of the last utilities in, and the shallowest.
Plan energisation ring by ring: each needs testing, an authority inspection, snag clearance and an energisation date. These are real activities with waiting time.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities are organised by MV ring and, inside each ring, by substation and its LV area — the same units in which the authority inspects and energises.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Standard site calendar. Authority inspections and energisations are dated activities on the authority's calendar, with a waiting time after each request.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Per substation: plinth / room → equipment set → terminations → tests. Per ring: road ducts → trenches → MV cable → joints → cable tests. A ring is energised only when all its substations and cables are tested and the authority has inspected it; LV areas follow their substation. The critical path follows equipment delivery or the last road section released for trenching.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: The authority approves the design in the assumed time; the primary substation has a spare feeder ready on the planned date; plots and roads are released for trenching in the planned order; approved jointers are available.

sections.heading: Procurement & long-lead items
sections.body: The schedule tracks the following as milestones because they drive the programme:

rows: Before equipment installation at each substation

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Cables share the utility corridor with water, telecom and lighting; minimum separations apply. Trenching follows deeper utilities and precedes kerbs and paving. Transformers need crane access to each plinth.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Main risks: late approval, late transformers or RMUs, damage to laid cables by other contractors, authority snags at inspection, and the upstream supply not ready. Contingency is held before the first energisation and before the final one.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 by MV ring and substation; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the trenching, cable and installation teams — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
